history.period: Legend dates the shrine to 300-400 years ago (verify)
history.summary: Shani Shingnapur's shrine is a swayambhu (self-emerged) five-and-a-half-foot black rock symbolising Lord Shani, installed on an open-air platform with a Trishula beside it and a Nandi image to the south. Legend says a shepherd found the stone bleeding on the banks of the Panasnala river after floods; Lord Shani appeared in a dream, identified himself, and instructed that the idol remain roofless under the open sky, promising the village protection - hence houses, shops and even the bank traditionally kept no doors or locks. It is regarded as a 'jagrut devasthan' (alive temple). The first recorded theft in the village occurred in 2010, with another in 2011. Following a 400-year tradition barring women from the inner sanctum, the Bombay High Court ruled on 30 March 2016 that women could not be denied temple entry; the Shani Shingnapur trust allowed women into the sanctum on 8 April 2016. The shrine gained wide popularity after the film Surya Putra Shanidev.

name: Shani Shingnapur Temple
town_description: Shani Shingnapur (also spelled Shinganapur) is a village in Nevasa taluka of Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra, about 35 km from Ahmednagar. It is world-famous for its roofless open-air shrine of Lord Shani and for its tradition of houses without doors or locks, trusting in the deity's protection. The village draws 30,000-45,000 visitors a day, swelling to around three lakh on Amavasya.

travel.airport: Shirdi International Airport (~65-75 km - verify); Aurangabad Airport is another option (~140 km - verify).
travel.road: ~35 km from Ahmednagar and ~72 km from Shirdi on the Sonai-Shani Shinganapur Road; guided day-tours run from Shirdi and Aurangabad.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Amavasya (new moon) days draw the largest crowds. Visit early morning or evening since the shrine is open-air.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): some sources report the temple open 24 hours with free entry; others report 5:30 AM-7:30 PM.
